John McGinn’s match-up vs 900k Celtic signing that made him realise ‘I am ready’ for the big time

Amir Mir
Tue 8 September 2026 21:30, UK

John McGinn and Celtic will forever be a ‘what if.’

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:04
Instaread

That saga, story, missed opportunity for Celtic, blessing in disguise for the player, however you want to call it, will forever be talked about until the end of time.

But while McGinn captains Aston Villa in the present day and is a crucial player for Scotland, it wasn’t all plain sailing for him when he was coming through at St Mirren as a teenager.

Speaking on the Overlap, McGinn explained how he would get ‘beat’ by the club’s goalkeeper in a bleep test, but not so long after, he would come up against Victor Wanyama at Hampden, and it made him realise, ‘I am ready’ for the big time.

John McGinn on facing Celtic great Victor Wanyama

“I still wasn’t that fit (when I got into the St Mirren team at 18),” shared McGinn.

“Craig Sampson, the keeper, he used to beat me in the bleep test. Whereas now I find that easy, the bleep test. But back then I used to struggle. I know I run weird. But I used to run like I was dragging a shovel. 

“Then a few injuries happened in the team, and I managed to break through. I remember my debut against Celtic; I think it was 5-0, we lost, but what a day, man! It was at St Mirren, but I got ten minutes. Managed to do pretty well, and then from there, I was involved most weeks.

MORE CELTIC STORIES

“I remember playing against Wanyama. My fifth start at Hampden. Absolutely bricking it. That’s when I started to realise, no, I am ready to play against these players. It was a great place to learn. I learned a lot of things that help me now as a captain at St Mirren.”

When McGinn faced Wanyama

Celtic signed Wanyama for £900k from Beerschot in 2011, and he went on to become one of the club’s best players of the modern era.

A no-nonsense powerhouse, it was no surprise that the Kenyan would eventually move to the English Premier League and continue to be a success there.

But the two games McGinn faced up against Wanyama at Hampden came in and around the same period.

The first was St Mirren’s 3-2 win over Celtic in the League Cup semi-final on January 27, 2013 – Neil Lennon was the Celtic boss, with Wanyama playing in the middle of the park alongside Scott Brown and Joe Ledley.

McGinn played 76 minutes for the Buddies, who were managed by Danny Lennon, as they pulled off a shock result.

Celtic would get revenge weeks later because they would beat St Mirren 2-1 in the Scottish Cup quarter-final at the same venue.

Once again, McGinn played in the middle of the park, up against Wanyama, with Anthony Stokes and Joe Ledley the goalscorers.
